title: Fiberwise relative initiality fills a boundary in a cartesian family
statement:
Use quasicategories, mapping spaces and standard simplices of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and cartesian fibrations and cartesian edges of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $S,\mathcal A,\mathcal D$ be quasicategories in a fixed universe, let $p:\mathcal A\to S$ and $q:\mathcal D\to S$ be cartesian fibrations, and let $R:\mathcal A\to\mathcal D$ be an inner fibration with $qR=p$ that carries $p$-cartesian edges to $q$-cartesian edges. Write $\mathcal A_s,\mathcal D_s$ for strict simplicial fibers and $R_s$ for the induced functor. Fix $n\geq1$, let $\partial\Delta^n$ be the union of the proper faces, and let
$$a:\partial\Delta^n\to\mathcal A,\qquad b:\Delta^n\to\mathcal D,\qquad Ra=b|_{\partial\Delta^n}.$$
Set $x=a(0)$ and $s=p(x)$. Suppose that for every $y\in\mathcal A_s$ the map
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal A_s}(x,y)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D_s}(R_sx,R_sy)$$
induced by $R_s$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Then there exists $\widetilde a:\Delta^n\to\mathcal A$ with $\widetilde a|_{\partial\Delta^n}=a$ and $R\widetilde a=b$ as exact simplicial equalities. No preservation of initial objects by the cartesian transport functors is assumed.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.5.19(2), promotion of fiberwise relative initiality through cartesian fibrations, followed by Corollary 7.1.5.17(1) <=> (3) (02WS), exact positive-dimensional boundary lifting. Relative initiality is stated explicitly as equivalence of outgoing mapping spaces. Both read online; not archived. Kerodon tags, not Stacks tags.

proof.text: Fix any vertex $z\in\mathcal A$, and put $t=p(z)$. Consider the map $\theta_z:\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal A}(x,z)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(Rx,Rz)$ over $B_z=\operatorname{Map}_S(s,t)$. For each vertex $f:s\to t$ of $B_z$, choose a $p$-cartesian lift $e:y\to z$ of $f$ with $p(y)=s$, using the target-lifting clause of the cartesian-fibration definition. Its image $R(e):Ry\to Rz$ is $q$-cartesian by hypothesis. Apply the cartesian-edge mapping-fiber formula to $(p,e,x)$ and $(q,R(e),Rx)$. It identifies the homotopy fibers of the two maps to $B_z$ over $f$ with $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal A_s}(x,y)$ and $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D_s}(R_sx,R_sy)$, respectively. The formula also supplies that all three total and base mapping spaces are Kan complexes.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 7.1.5.19(2), choice of cartesian lift; mapping-fiber identification from Proposition 5.1.3.11.

proof.text: Apply the naturality clause of the mapping-fiber formula to $R$, which is a functor over $S$ preserving the chosen cartesian edge. Under the two displayed identifications the induced map on homotopy fibers is exactly the map induced by $R_s$ on maps from $x$ to $y$, up to the specified homotopy. It is therefore a weak homotopy equivalence by the hypothesis on $x$. Now apply homotopy-fiber detection to the square with top map $\theta_z$ and bottom map $1_{B_z}$ (the square commutes because $qR=p$). Every homotopy-fiber map is an equivalence and $1_{B_z}$ is an equivalence, so $\theta_z$ is an equivalence. This holds for every $z$; no claim about transporting initial objects was used.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 7.1.5.19(2), fiberwise test for the outgoing total mapping-space map.

proof.text: Apply the relative-initial boundary characterization with $p=R$, $\mathcal X=\mathcal A$, $\mathcal Y=\mathcal D$ and the vertex $x=a(0)$. The stated inner-fibration hypothesis on $R$ is exactly its lifting hypothesis; step 2 proves its outgoing mapping-space condition for every vertex $z\in\mathcal A$. Its positive-dimensional boundary-lifting clause now applies to the specified $n\geq1$, $a$ and $b$, since $Ra=b|_{\partial\Delta^n}$ and $a(0)=x$. It supplies $\widetilde a$ with both exact equations $R\widetilde a=b$ and $\widetilde a|_{\partial\Delta^n}=a$. This includes $n=1$; no dimension-zero lifting is needed.
